en-US.author: nub contributors
en-US.description: The all-in-one JavaScript toolkit that augments Node.js instead of trying to replace it.
en-US.longDescription: An all-in-one toolkit for Node.js. One Rust binary to run your files and scripts, install dependencies, and manage Node itself — a Bun-like modern DX on top of the node you already have. There's no new runtime to adopt and no lock-in: every augmentation rides on Node's own public extension surfaces.
en-US.name: Nub
en-US.releaseNotes:
Nub 0.11.0 preloads TypeScript 7.1 content mappers, adds nub add --save-types, installs one copy of a package where pnpm does, and removes the canary channel. It also fixes a broad set of correctness bugs in the runtime, the package manager and nub run.
Important
Five changes can surface in an existing project:
- The canary channel is gone. nub upgrade --canary and --stable are unknown flags, and install.sh and install.ps1 no longer accept canary. An existing canary install keeps working, and nub upgrade --stable still moves it to a release (#1102)
- A lockfile missing a required entry is broken. nub ci and nub install --frozen-lockfile exit 16 and name the entry, and a plain nub install repairs it. Both exited 0 and left a tree that could not load (#1105)
- nub add <pkg>@<tag> saves a prerelease exact, as pnpm does. A stable tag still saves with ^ (#1096)
- Some lockfiles change once. A local or URL package keeps its peers on its key, and a tree that held duplicate copies of a package collapses them on its next fresh resolve (#1093, #1089)
- The first install after upgrading relinks once, because the dependency scan's cache was reset (#1113)
Content mappers
TypeScript 7.1's content mappers type-check other file types, but TypeScript never runs them. Nub now preloads the ./register export of every package the tsconfig lists, with no --import and no nub.jsonc entry (#1082).
{
  // ...
  "contentMappers": [
    { "package": "motherload", "extensions": [".toml", ".yaml"] }
  ]
}
import config from "./config.yaml"; // loaded by motherload/register
extends and references are followed, the longest extension answers first, and an entry's options reach its register in CONTENT_MAPPER_OPTIONS.

Type packages on add
nub add --save-types <pkg> also saves the DefinitelyTyped package to devDependencies for each registry package whose installed version ships no types, picking the newest @types release on that package's major (#1110, fixes #1016).
nub add --save-types express
A package with no @types release, or only a deprecated stub, prints skipped @types/<name>: <reason>. An @types entry the project already lists is kept.
